text:
maria: quick status — brought up hyperon-13b int6 on a small traffic sample (2k requests) vs existing int8 baseline. wanted to surface early cost/quality delta and get routing recs.

ajay: nice. quick numbers?

maria: TL;DR: ~28% token-cost reduction, median tail latency -18ms, but convo-level F1 on our deveval drops ~3.5 points on mult-turn QA prompts. single-turn QA mostly stable. raws below.

katie: can you paste the eval breakdown (by prompt length / turn count)?

maria: pasted aggregate below (high level):
```
sample: 2k requests (mixed prod-sim traffic)
int8: cost_per_1k_tokens = $1.00, median_latency = 120ms, convo_f1 = 78.6
int6: cost_per_1k_tokens = $0.72, median_latency = 102ms, convo_f1 = 75.1
delta: -$0.28 per 1k tokens, -15% cost, -3.5 F1, -18ms latency
```

maria: breakdown: short prompts (<128 tokens): F1 delta ~0.4 points; medium (128-512): ~1.8 points; long (>512 or >3 turns): ~6-7 points drop.

sam: interesting — so most degradation concentrated in longer context / multi-turn. is KV-cache behavior identical between quant modes? could be precision bleed on long seqs.

maria: KV cache config unchanged. we dumped sample logits and topk diffs for a few failing traces, looks like higher perplexity and more hallucinations on int6 for some biology/legal anchors.

ajay: any specific template or prompt family that regressed hardest?

maria: yes — multi-step instruction with chain-of-thought style, and extraction tasks that rely on exact spans. I'll attach 5 redacted examples to the thread.

katie: for product/GTN guidance we should propose a traffic-splitting policy: default int6 for short interactions and non-sensitive domains, fallback to int8 for long sessions or high-regret prompts. also flag risky templates to always go to int8.

maria: that was my thinking. quick sim for routing rules: route_to_int8 if (estimated_total_tokens > 600) OR (turn_count >= 4) OR (category in ["legal", "medical"]). small sample shows this recovers ~85% of the F1 gap while still saving ~12% cost vs baseline.

sam: idea: try hybrid quant config — keep first N layers at int8 (or fp16) and rest int6. bringup might be heavier but could close the long-tail regression. has anyone tried hybrid with hyperon?

ajay: not on hyperon yet. we did a quick hybrid on a 7b and saw long-context stability improved. Ops note: hybrid increases memory footprint and may reduce token throughput; need perf bench.

maria: can run hybrid on 3-node dev cluster. ask infra to spin nodes with slightly larger RAM. @devops-bot can you provision 3x a40-dev nodes?

devops-bot: request received: provisioning 3x a40-dev nodes (est 14m). I'll post when ready. :spinner:

katie: also worth a quick eval on subjective quality metrics (toxicity / safety) — sometimes quant shifts amplify rare failure modes. we should include automated safety checks in the scorecard before recommending broad rollout.

maria: Agreed. current scorecard fields I'm planning: conv_f1, exact-match, latency median/95, cost per 1k tokens, regression_count (by template), safety_flags, top-10 hallucinated entities. will share proto.

ajay: for GTN pitch, recommend: 1) default int6 for sessions with <128 tokens or single-turn chat; 2) route long / >=4 turns or category flagged to int8; 3) pilot hybrid-int layers for >512 tokens use-case; 4) monitor eval suite and auto-rollback if regression >2.5 F1 on critical templates.

sam: nit: set the rollback threshold per-template, not global — some templates tolerate regresses, others (billing/legal) should be 0 tolerance.

maria: noted. i'll produce a short routing config snippet and expected unit-econ impact.

maria: unit econ sim (approx):
```
baseline int8: $1.00 per 1k tokens
naive switch to int6 everywhere: $0.72 per 1k tokens (saves $0.28)
proposed routing: mix = 60% int6 / 40% int8 -> blended cost = $0.832 per 1k tokens (~16.8% saving)
hybrid fallback (for long context) increases cost of those requests by ~8% but keeps quality.
```

katie: sounds actionable. next steps?

maria: 1) devops-bot spins nodes (in flight). 2) i'll run hybrid-int6-int8 experiment and attach eval diffs (expect 48h). 3) katie/sam to draft routing rules for GTN, include per-template rollback thresholds. 4) set safety checks in the scorecard pipeline.

ajay: add perf/latency guardrail: require 95p latency < 300ms for web-tier to accept route.

maria: added. thanks all. will post interim results in this thread. :thumbsup:

katie: thanks — please tag me when hybrid results ready.

sam: ping me on the failing traces, I can help triage the logits diffs.

maria: will do. end of update.
